title: Ahab
lead: Ahab son of Omri, king of Israel about 874–853 BC, married Jezebel of Sidon, built a temple of Baal in Samaria and clashed with Elijah. Kings calls him the worst king before him, yet he was a strong ruler who appears in Assyrian records with the largest chariot force at Qarqar.

sections.h: Ahab in the Bible and in history
sections.b:
Kings introduces Ahab with a harsh verdict: he did more evil than all before him, married Jezebel and served Baal (1 Kings 16:30–33). His reign fills the rest of 1 Kings: the drought and Carmel (1 Kings 17–18), wars with Aram (1 Kings 20), Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21) and his death at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22). His house falls to Jehu (2 Kings 9–10), and Micah later condemns the people for keeping the practices of Ahab's house (Micah 6:16).

Outside the Bible, Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith lists "Ahab the Israelite" with 2,000 chariots and 10,000 soldiers at Qarqar in 853 BC. The Mesha Stele says that Omri and his son oppressed Moab. The palaces and ivories of Samaria and the royal enclosure at Jezreel show the wealth of the Omride kings. Historians therefore see a capable and powerful king, judged by the Bible for his religion more than for his politics.
